newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates up on mill owners' buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates up on mill owners' buying.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates jumped on Monday on selective buying by mill owners on fears that the arrival of the 1997/98 (July-June) crop may be delayed by rains, dealers said.

"The mill owners are going for good-quality stocks as they fear that there may be a slight delay in the arrival of new crop," dealer Nasim Usman said. "Exporters remained on the sidelines and are buyers only at lower levels."
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded between 2,050 ($50.62) and 2,150 rupees per maund (37.32 k.g.), dealers said.
